coverage_summary.tests_collected_breakdown_note: 29 unique test functions; pytest parametrize expansion adds 5 extra cases (4 from test_cpe_stripped_for_each_non_nvd_ecosystem, 1 from test_parent_cves_remain_detectable_through_enhanced_mapper)

decisions: Dispatch counts and expected vulnerability id sets in the mixed/pyPI-only scenarios are read from step1b_mock_scenarios.json (scenario_enh_001 and scenario_enh_002) rather than inlined as constants.

Expected OSV/GHSA advisory ids in per-ecosystem dispatch tests are pulled from the fixture record by ecosystem filter (e.g. `r['affected'][0]['package']['ecosystem'] == 'Go'`) rather than typed directly.

The CPE-pollution exemplar test iterates step1b_mock_entities.json entities.CPEPollutionExemplar[] and asserts each fixture's expected_post_sanitization_component, so adding a new exemplar entry expands coverage automatically with no test edit.

Ecosystem membership in cpe-strip tests is derived from dispatch_table['nvd_ecosystems'] at runtime — adding 'nuget' to that list would automatically extend the CPE-retention guarantee without touching the test.
Fabricated CPE strings in the integration test are synthesised from each dep's name and exact_version, so new fixtures contribute new components without per-component test code.
remaining_hardcoded_values_and_rationale: Exception class names (OSVCacheNotSyncedError, GHSACacheNotSyncedError) — these ARE the contract; cannot be parameterised away.
Log code substrings ('sync', 'unknownftype', 'not-a-purl-at-all', 'mystery-pkg') — these are the literal test inputs the BDD scenarios assert on.

Five parametrize cases in test_cpe_stripped_for_each_non_nvd_ecosystem inline (ecosystem, purl, fabricated_cpe) triples — these are intentionally enumerated because the test asserts coverage of the OSV+GHSA ecosystem set.
PURL string 'pkg:npm/express@4.18.2' in idempotency clean-lookup test — this is a deliberately-absent PURL used to assert that lookup returns empty on miss.

red_phase_expectations.reason: step6_tdd_green_phase_business.py does not exist in the enhancement directory yet. The import block in step4_atdd_business.py catches the ImportError and routes every test to _require_implementation() which calls pytest.fail with a clear message naming the missing module and classes.
red_phase_expectations.first_run_expected_outcome: 29 failures (or 34 with parametrize expansion), each with the message 'Step 6 implementation not yet present in enhancement directory...'

scope_boundary_assertions: Parent session files under outputs/sessions/SBOM-20260409-sb01/ that are not under enhancements/ are NOT modified or imported directly by this test file.
Tests use a local nvd_cache_seed fixture (dict-of-dicts) rather than importing parent NVDCacheManager, keeping the enhancement test suite hermetic.
test_enhancement_module_does_not_import_live_network_libraries enforces the 'No Live Network In CI' rule by parsing the Step 6 module source for forbidden imports.

next_step_inputs_required: Step 5 (red phase 1) will use this file as the acceptance bar; Step 6 (green phase 1) will create step6_tdd_green_phase_business.py to make these tests pass.

key_contracts.EcosystemVulnerabilityMapper.__init__: (nvd_cache: dict, osv_cache: OSVCache, ghsa_cache: GHSACache, dispatch_table: dict)
